errors.why_wrong: The ovarian axis uses pulsatile GnRH. TRH regulates the thyroid axis. [Source](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK499898/)
This arrow should represent FSH or LH. TSH primarily stimulates the thyroid gland. [Source](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK499898/)
This arrow should represent LH or FSH. ACTH primarily stimulates the adrenal cortex. [Source](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK499898/)

errors.what: “Estradiol and progesterone suppress GnRH, LH and FSH for most of the cycle.”
errors.why_wrong: This makes progesterone seem like a major suppressor throughout the cycle, although its inhibitory role is chiefly luteal; estradiol is central to follicular-phase feedback. [Source](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK279070/)

errors.what: “Inhibin B from granulosa cells suppresses FSH only” describes the dotted loop without a cycle phase.
errors.why_wrong: Inhibin B is prominent in the follicular phase, while inhibin A predominates in the luteal phase. The unqualified label can imply that B is the ovarian inhibin throughout the cycle. [Source](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK279054/)

errors.what: The solid negative-feedback and dashed positive-feedback paths both end in ordinary arrowheads.
errors.why_wrong: Their opposing effects are conveyed only by distant text and line style; the arrowheads themselves can look like stimulation in both cases.

errors.what: The diagram and legend labels are very small, and most of the PNG below the figure is blank.
errors.why_wrong: The labels are difficult to read at the supplied size, and the unused space makes the teaching diagram appear smaller.

verdict: The three main forward-axis labels name hormones from other endocrine axes. Although the feedback paths broadly match the caption, the picture does not correctly show GnRH driving LH and FSH.
